To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The A protein of the tryptohphan operon is synthesized at a rate proportional to the amount of tryptophan available to the cell.
two frameshift mutations in trpA recombine to give an altered tryptophan-synthetase A protein.

the trpA gene is expressed independently of the other genes in the operon during tryptophant starvation, and that the tryptophanylation of A protein is the result of the synthesis of a tryptophanyl-tRNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the tryptopan operon of E.coli.
the regulation of the tryptrophic enzymes in Escherichia Coli, with special emphasis on the regulation of the A gene product of the operon.
the expression of the trpA gene during tryptophanthan starvation in Escherichia colt.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tryptophan is not required for expression of the trpA gene in E. coli.
the tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase of E. coli K12 has an absolute specificity for tryptophan and is unable to accept other amino acids in place of tryptophan.
the A protein of E. coli is not a feedback-regulated enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trpA gene is capable of independent expression.

tryptophan synthesis in the wild-type strain is controlled at the level of transcription of the tryptphan operon, whereas in the mutant strains the synthesis of A protein is controlled at the translation level.
the tryptophanyl tRNA is able to recognize a unique tryptopal residue inserted into the tryptophanylsynthetase A protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the trpA gene is expressed independently of the trpB gene in tryptophan-starved cells.

the tryptophans are not essential for the activity of the tryptopan synthase A protein, but they are essential for the activity in the tryptophane synthase B protein, which is the enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of tryptophan to indole and serine.
the trpA gene can be independently expressed during tryptophant starvation.
